answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. This is resilient because unearned rewards are capped and eventually burned, so an attacker cannot bank on a runaway Sybil campaign paying off. Consider a grove as the anchor of the cost. A marble stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a wander holds...
